question_text: What should you reckon with when approaching children?

options.text: Rash behaviour on the part of the children
Fast and correct reactions of the children
Proper road conduct of the children

correct_answers.text: Rash behaviour on the part of the children

comment: Children can always behave ill-considered and are therefore exempt from the principle of trust towards other road users. Thus, when children approach you, you must reduce your speed to be ready to brake.

question_text: What conduct must you expect of children at zebra crossings?

options.text: They will run onto the zebra crossing without paying attention to traffic
They will turn around on the zebra crossing for no apparent reason and run back
They will wait at the curb because they always correctly judge the speed and distance of approaching vehicles

correct_answers.text: They will run onto the zebra crossing without paying attention to traffic
They will turn around on the zebra crossing for no apparent reason and run back

comment: Children generally do not have the necessary training to always behave according to the rules in road traffic. Therefore, it is quite conceivable that they do not know the meaning of a zebra crossing and enter the road despite approaching vehicles or suddenly run back after crossing.

question_text: What must you do?

options.text: Brake heavily immediately and remain ready to brake
Continue at the same speed because the children will certainly stop
Proceed at the same speed so as not to obstruct the traffic following behind

correct_answers.text: Brake heavily immediately and remain ready to brake

comment: If a child suddenly runs across the road without paying attention to the traffic, you should immediately slow down and continue driving ready to brake. Also, make sure that other children follow. It is essential to stay at walking pace to be able to stop completely if necessary.

question_text:
What do you have to reckon with when children are waiting at traffic lights?
That the children

options.text: - will already start running when the traffic lights in my driving direction change from green to amber
- will also start running when the light is red because they cannot wait since it's taking them too long
- will push each other onto the roadway

correct_answers.text: - will already start running when the traffic lights in my driving direction change from green to amber
- will also start running when the light is red because they cannot wait since it's taking them too long
- will push each other onto the roadway

comment: Due to a lack of life experience as well as insufficient education, children do not always behave according to the rules in road traffic and, for example, get into the lane during a scuffle. Furthermore, you must expect children to suddenly run across the road, even if the traffic lights are still red or the lights of the cross-traffic are just changing.

question_text:
A group of children are cycling on a cycle path that ends. What do you have to reckon with?
That the children

options.text: - will move onto the roadway without paying attention
- will move too far onto the roadway
- will get off their bicycles and wait until the roadway is clear

correct_answers.text: - will move onto the roadway without paying attention
- will move too far onto the roadway

comment: Children in particular, who are generally not overly familiar with traffic rules, tend to make unpredictable manoeuvres. Therefore, especially at the end of a cycle path, you should be aware that the young road users could drive onto the road without warning. Furthermore, it often happens that children ride in groups next to each other and thus partially swerve into your lane.

question_text: Which statements are correct?

options.text: You may pass on the right-hand side at walking speed provided that passengers are not obstructed and you are sure no-one is endangered
If no-one is obstructed or endangered, you may pass on the right-hand side at a speed faster than walking speed
Passengers must allow moving traffic to pass before boarding

correct_answers.text: You may pass on the right-hand side at walking speed provided that passengers are not obstructed and you are sure no-one is endangered

comment: If you do not obstruct or endanger the passengers getting on or off the tram, you may pass the stopping tram slowly at walking speed. It is important to note that passengers have absolute priority in this situation and do not have to let moving traffic pass. If necessary, you as the vehicle driver must stop and wait.

question_text:
What must you heed in this situation?
You may

options.text: - not overtake the bus while it is still moving
- pass the stationary bus at walking speed provided you are sure that passengers are not endangered
- overtake the bus while it is still moving

correct_answers.text: - not overtake the bus while it is still moving
- pass the stationary bus at walking speed provided you are sure that passengers are not endangered

comment: If a public bus or school bus has its hazard lights on and is still moving, you must not overtake it. If the bus has come to a halt at the stop, you may pass at walking pace and at an appropriate distance. This is necessary in order not to endanger the passengers getting on and off the bus. If you are travelling in the opposite lane, you must also slow down or stop to ensure the safety of the passengers.

question_text: What do you have to reckon with when elderly persons using walking frames cross the road?

options.text: They may stop on the road
They may turn round and go back
They will cross the road slowly

correct_answers.text: They may stop on the road
They may turn round and go back
They will cross the road slowly

comment: When elderly people with walking aids cross the road, you have a higher duty of care. The principle of trust is suspended. You must expect these people to stop suddenly or turn around unexpectedly. Older people also take a comparatively long time to cross the road.

question_text: A person in a wheelchair is travelling along the road although there is a pavement on the right. What do you do?

options.text: I follow behind the wheelchair until I can overtake it
I overtake it, leaving plenty of room on the side because the wheelchair may swing out
I honk the horn to indicate that the person is not behaving correctly

correct_answers.text: I follow behind the wheelchair until I can overtake it
I overtake it, leaving plenty of room on the side because the wheelchair may swing out

comment: Disabled and elderly people sometimes do not behave in a roadworthy manner due to physical limitations. Therefore, please be especially careful and be sure to show consideration. Expect the wheelchair user to suddenly and unexpectedly swerve and drive even further into the lane. In such situations, it is not permitted to use the horn or drive around the person at high speed.

question_text: Having crossed the road, a person in a wheelchair cannot get up the curb and onto the pavement. What do you do?

options.text: I stop and switch on the hazard warning lights
I get out of the car and help the person in the wheelchair
I honk the horn and drive around the person

correct_answers.text: I stop and switch on the hazard warning lights
I get out of the car and help the person in the wheelchair

comment: You should help the person. To do this, you may stop and switch on the hazard warning lights to warn other road users of possible dangers. It is not permitted to honk your horn and drive around the person in this situation. This would frighten and unsettle the wheelchair user.

question_text: Who has a severe visual handicap?

options.text: The man
The child
The woman

correct_answers.text: The man

comment: You must expect a severe visual impairment in the case of persons with the following markings: If a person is wearing a yellow armband with three black dots and/or a white blind person's cane extended diagonally.

question_text: What do you do?

options.text: Stop
Let the man cross the road
Make eye contact with the man

correct_answers.text: Stop
Let the man cross the road

comment: Visually impaired pedestrians often wear an armband and have a guide dog with a white driving harness with them. It is not possible to make eye contact with a visually impaired road user. Therefore, you are obliged to show special consideration here. You must stop to allow the pedestrian to cross the road safely.

question_text: What must you be aware of?

options.text: Pedestrians crossing the road in front of the bus
People crossing the road from left to right to get to the bus
The bus will reverse suddenly

correct_answers.text: Pedestrians crossing the road in front of the bus
People crossing the road from left to right to get to the bus

comment: Where buses or trams wait at stops, you must always assume that people will suddenly step onto the road. Some passengers run quickly across the street to reach the bus. When passengers get off the bus, they often enter the lane surprisingly without paying attention to the traffic. Because the reversing light is not lit, you as the driver behind you can be sure that the bus will leave the bus stop driving forwards.

question_text:
What risks must you be aware of?
[The boy] on the bicycle will

options.text: - proceed onto the road
- continue on the cycle path
- stop moving

correct_answers.text: - proceed onto the road

comment: Cyclists do not always behave in a way that is appropriate for traffic. Here, even if the child has previously looked to your left, he or she could ride onto the roadway. To avoid a dangerous situation, you should therefore reduce your speed and be ready to brake.

question_text: How do you behave?

options.text: watch out for children
be ready to brake
continue driving at the same speed

correct_answers.text: watch out for children
be ready to brake

comment: Reduce speed and watch the two children very closely. Be careful and ready to brake. Stop if the children's behaviour makes this necessary.

question_text:
What must you be aware of?
The cyclist in front of me will

options.text: - turn to the left
- go to the other side of the road
- not impede me as I proceed

correct_answers.text: - turn to the left
- go to the other side of the road

comment: It is always possible that cyclists do not behave in a way that is appropriate for the traffic. A cyclist could turn left or change sides of the road without indicating this with a hand signal. If there are two cyclists, it is possible that the second will also follow the first without hand signals. Therefore, you should be ready to brake even if the cyclists continue straight ahead.

question_text: What risks must you be aware of?

options.text: the children will not get off the road in time
some children will turn around again
all children will wait on the pavement

correct_answers.text: the children will not get off the road in time
some children will turn around again

comment: If a ball is lying on the road, it can be assumed that a child will come and fetch it. For you as a driver, this means: stop immediately so that the child can fetch the ball safely. With children, you have to expect that they will behave in a way that is contrary to traffic regulations and that they will not be able to assess dangers correctly.

question_text: How should you behave?

options.text: slow to walking pace
remain ready to brake
continue driving at same speed

correct_answers.text: slow to walking pace
remain ready to brake

comment: The rule here is: reduce speed immediately, be ready to brake and drive slowly past the situation. It can be assumed that children who are playing are not paying attention to the traffic and are not behaving in a way that is appropriate for the traffic.

question_text: How must you behave?

options.text: slow to walking pace immediately
remain ready to brake
drive past at the same speed

correct_answers.text: slow to walking pace immediately
remain ready to brake

comment: Most likely, a child will come running into the road after the ball without paying attention to the traffic. Immediately slow your vehicle down to walking speed. Be especially alert and ready to brake!

question_text:
In this situation, which vehicles may drive past, at walking speed only, while ensuring there is no danger to any passengers?
All vehicles that

options.text: - are travelling in the same direction
- are oncoming

correct_answers.text: - are travelling in the same direction
- are oncoming

comment: When the hazard warning lights of a bus are switched on at a bus stop, all vehicles in both directions must pass the bus at walking speed. There shall be no danger to or obstruction of passengers boarding or alighting the bus.

question_text: What should you do now?

options.text: I slow down to walking pace
I remain ready to brake
I overtake [the cyclist]

correct_answers.text: I slow down to walking pace
I remain ready to brake

comment: Since there are children both on the left and right on the street, you should brake to walking pace and remain ready to brake.

question_text: What should you do in this situation?

options.text: I perform an emergency braking manoeuvre
I sound my horn and continue driving
I accelerate

correct_answers.text: I perform an emergency braking manoeuvre

comment: Immediately perform emergency braking to prevent a collision with the cyclist coming from the left. Continuing to ride would be dangerous in the situation, even though the traffic lights are green in your direction.

question_text: Why must you drive slowly here and be ready to brake?

options.text: Because the traffic situation is confusing
Because there is a child on the carriageway
Because [the white van] is moving off

correct_answers.text: Because the traffic situation is confusing
Because there is a child on the carriageway

comment: The child behind the van on the left runs towards the roadway. You cannot see whether it will stop. Therefore, be especially attentive and careful in this unclear traffic situation. Drive slowly and be ready to brake.

question_text: What is the correct course of action in this situation?

options.text: I stop and allow the person to cross the road
I drive to the left past the person, leaving sufficient clearance space
I flash my headlights to signal to the person that I am giving way

correct_answers.text: I stop and allow the person to cross the road

comment: The man is wearing a yellow armband and has a guide dog with him. He is blind or visually impaired and cannot see the traffic situation. Special care must be taken for blind people. Therefore, you must let him cross the road in front of you.

question_text:
Why must you anticipate that children might behave unpredictably in road traffic situations?
Because children

options.text: - are easily distracted
- are frequently unable to fully grasp the road traffic situation
- are frequently unable to correctly detect the direction from which a sound is coming

correct_answers.text: - are easily distracted
- are frequently unable to fully grasp the road traffic situation
- are frequently unable to correctly detect the direction from which a sound is coming

comment:
Children often behave unpredictably, which is why other road users always have to count on the unexpected. Due to external stimuli in the environment, small children are constantly distracted from the road and traffic. They continuously let their eyes hike in the area and get stuck with interesting events or objects. The noise perception also only develops in the course of life and is only available to a limited extent in children. That is why children can usually not assign the many noises in road traffic to a certain direction and it is more difficult for them to assess them purely acoustically from which direction a vehicle approaches.
In addition to the perception of the direction, the perception of distances, speeds and braking distance in childhood is not yet fully pronounced. Therefore, children can often only overlook the traffic situation incompletely.

question_text: A child is walking on the pavement with a dog on a lead. Can this cause a dangerous situation?

options.text: Yes, if the dog suddenly runs onto the roadway and pulls the child along behind
Yes, if the dog tears away and the child runs after the dog
No, because dogs are afraid of traffic

correct_answers.text: Yes, if the dog suddenly runs onto the roadway and pulls the child along behind
Yes, if the dog tears away and the child runs after the dog

comment: Dangerous situations can arise here. The dog could break loose, and the child could run after him. It would also be conceivable that the dog would run onto the road, and the child would pull along. They should, therefore, drive slowly and be ready to brake.

question_text:
What must you heed in this situation?
You may

options.text: - pass at walking speed only
- pass only if you are sure that passengers are not endangered
- not pass under any circumstances

correct_answers.text: - pass at walking speed only
- pass only if you are sure that passengers are not endangered

comment: When public transport and school buses are at a stop and their hazard warning lights are switched on, the following applies: Vehicles may only pass them at walking speed and at a sufficient distance. This applies to oncoming traffic as well as to vehicles travelling in the same direction as the bus. Any danger to passengers must be ruled out by you as the driver of the vehicle.

question_text: Which statements are correct in this situation?

options.text: Cars coming from the opposite direction may pass the bus provided that they do so with care
You may pass the bus provided that you do so with care
As you are coming from the opposite direction, you do not need to worry about the bus

correct_answers.text: Cars coming from the opposite direction may pass the bus provided that they do so with care
You may pass the bus provided that you do so with care

comment: Vehicles coming from both directions may only pass public buses, school buses and trams stopped at bus stops with caution. As the bus has not switched on its hazard warning lights, you do not have to slow your vehicle down to walking speed. Be especially attentive in the situation!

question_text: Which statements are correct in this situation?

options.text: The bus may be passed in either lane but no faster than at walking speed
Vehicles in both lanes must stop if passengers would otherwise be endangered
The vehicles in the left lane may pass the bus without paying any special attention

correct_answers.text: The bus may be passed in either lane but no faster than at walking speed
Vehicles in both lanes must stop if passengers would otherwise be endangered

comment: If a bus is at a stop and its hazard warning lights are switched on, you as the driver may only pass the bus at walking speed on the same carriageway. Keep a sufficient distance. If necessary, you must stop and wait. The reason for this is the safety of bus passengers, which must always be ensured. This also applies to road users travelling in oncoming traffic on the same carriageway.

question_text: In a residential area a ball rolls out in front of your vehicle. How must you react?

options.text: Brake
Continue driving
Avoid hitting it

correct_answers.text: Brake

comment: If a ball rolls in front of your vehicle in a residential area, you must expect a child to suddenly run into the road. You must therefore brake and be ready to stop, as the principle of trust does not apply in this case.

question_text: You are approaching children playing on the pavement. How must you behave?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to brake
Continue driving as before so as not to impede the traffic behind you
Sound your horn and continue driving

correct_answers.text: Slow down and be ready to brake

comment: Children playing on the pavement could unexpectedly run onto the roadway. The principle of trust is therefore suspended. You must reduce speed and be ready to brake.

question_text:
What should you anticipate in this situation?
The dog

options.text: - will run onto the carriageway, pulling the child behind it
- will break free and the child will run after it
- will be kept securely under control by the child

correct_answers.text: - will run onto the carriageway, pulling the child behind it
- will break free and the child will run after it

comment: In this situation, you should be prepared for the danger of the dog running into the lane and dragging the child behind it, and of the dog breaking loose and the child running after it.

question_text: In this situation, do you have to proceed slowly and be ready to brake?

options.text: Yes, because passengers could cross the road from in front of the bus
Yes, because pedestrians not alighting from the bus could cross the road
Yes, because the bus will begin moving immediately

correct_answers.text: Yes, because passengers could cross the road from in front of the bus
Yes, because pedestrians not alighting from the bus could cross the road

comment: As the bus is at the stop and flashing on the right, you should only drive past it very carefully. In addition, there is a person standing directly in front of the bus and thus in your immediate vicinity. You must also expect passengers to get off the bus. Other people may approach the bus from the other side of the road and want to get on. You should therefore slow down in any case so that you can brake immediately if necessary.

question_text:
The tram has just become stationary at the stop. What is the right course of action?
Passengers boarding or alighting

options.text: - may not be endangered
- may not be impeded
- may be warned using the horn

correct_answers.text: - may not be endangered
- may not be impeded

comment: You may carefully pass a stopping tram at walking speed - but only if this does not endanger or obstruct any passengers.

question_text:
Why must you pause here?
Because of

options.text: - the child
- the motorbike
- the off-road vehicle

correct_answers.text: - the child

comment: It's not clear what the child will do. It would be possible for the child to run onto the road without paying attention to the traffic. Therefore, you must carefully pass through: You should drive very slowly and be ready to brake.

question_text: What should you do?

options.text: Slow to walking pace
Remain ready to brake
Continue driving as before

correct_answers.text: Slow to walking pace
Remain ready to brake

comment: Special caution is always required towards children in road traffic. In this situation, you must expect that the small child will continue to drive onto the road behind the van. Slow down to walking speed and remain alert and ready to brake at all times. Stop if necessary if you are not sure how the child will behave. It would be grossly negligent to just honk your horn and drive on.

question_text: What should you do?

options.text: Brake early, to clearly indicate to the pedestrians that I am allowing them to cross
Continue driving, even if the pedestrians stop briefly
Arc around the pedestrians, to avoid impeding the following traffic

correct_answers.text: Brake early, to clearly indicate to the pedestrians that I am allowing them to cross

comment: Pedestrians always have absolute priority at pedestrian crossings. Therefore, brake your vehicle in good time and in a clearly visible manner. This way, pedestrians can easily see that you are fulfilling your obligation to wait and that they can enter the roadway. Even if the pedestrians are still standing at the roadside, it would be absolutely forbidden to simply drive on.

question_text: What should you do?

options.text: Wait to allow pedestrians to cross the road
Continue driving, because there is sufficient time before the pedestrians have reached my side of the road
Continue driving, because there are pedestrians on the left side of the road only

correct_answers.text: Wait to allow pedestrians to cross the road

comment: When pedestrians wait at a zebra crossing to cross the road, they have priority. This also applies if they are on the left-hand side of the road. You should therefore brake in good time. Pedestrians must be able to see that you are complying with your obligation to stop. Even if the pedestrians stop first and wait, you must give them the right of way in a clearly visible manner.

question_text: What actions should you anticipate at such stops?

options.text: Pedestrians will step off the tram-stop island unheedingly
Pedestrians will run across the road to the tram-stop island
Pedestrians will wait until the road is clear

correct_answers.text: Pedestrians will step off the tram-stop island unheedingly
Pedestrians will run across the road to the tram-stop island

comment: Pedestrians are required to wait at such traffic islands. You are therefore allowed to pass the tram even if the tram doors are still open. But because people often behave carelessly when getting on and off the tram, dangerous situations arise time and again. For example, without paying attention to the traffic, passengers simply run across the carriageway to reach the tram.

question_text: You want to turn right. What must you be prepared for?

options.text: The truck will stop
[The pedestrian] could let the truck pass by and then cross the road in front of me
After the truck has taken the turn, pedestrians could approach from the opposite side of the road

correct_answers.text: The truck will stop
[The pedestrian] could let the truck pass by and then cross the road in front of me
After the truck has taken the turn, pedestrians could approach from the opposite side of the road

comment: If you want to turn right, road users travelling in a straight line here have priority. These may be pedestrians or cyclists who want to cross the road. If a truck turns right in front of you, it is also possible that a pedestrian will let it pass. In that case, the lorry would block your view of the other side of the road and thus of the road users travelling from there.

question_text: What must you be prepared for?

options.text: For persons crossing
For visual obstructions
For vehicle doors opening

correct_answers.text: For persons crossing
For visual obstructions
For vehicle doors opening

comment: Where there are many parked cars, you should always drive carefully and considerately. On the one hand, your view is obstructed by the parked vehicles. Secondly, you must always be aware that car doors may be carelessly opened. Other road users may also want to cross the lane between the parked cars.

question_text: What should you anticipate?

options.text: That adults could walk onto the road
That children could appear between the vehicles
That it could be necessary to brake heavily

correct_answers.text: That adults could walk onto the road
That children could appear between the vehicles
That it could be necessary to brake heavily

comment: The "Children" danger sign on the right makes it clear that increased attention and a special degree of caution are necessary at this point. In addition to children, adults can of course also suddenly step onto the roadway between parked vehicles here, requiring heavy braking.

question_text: Why are older pedestrians at more risk than younger ones from road traffic?

options.text: They frequently have poorer sight and hearing
They frequently react more slowly and are less mobile
They frequently misjudge the speed of vehicles

correct_answers.text: They frequently have poorer sight and hearing
They frequently react more slowly and are less mobile
They frequently misjudge the speed of vehicles

comment: Older road users see less well, hear less well, react more slowly and misjudge the speed of vehicles. Be prepared for these people to recognise dangers too late and react too late or not at all.

question_text: What must you be aware of in residential areas with low traffic volumes?

options.text: That children playing run onto the road
That cyclists are inattentive
That all adults obey the road traffic regulations

correct_answers.text: That children playing run onto the road
That cyclists are inattentive

comment: In residential areas, low traffic levels often give children and adults a feeling of high safety. Some road users are thoughtless here, which often leads to inappropriate traffic behaviour. In such areas, always expect children playing, inattentive cyclists and pedestrians suddenly entering the road. Drive particularly carefully and attentively, as children in particular are unable to properly assess the dangers of road traffic.

question_text: What actions should you anticipate from persons at the pedestrian crossing?

options.text: They will look neither left nor right
They will unexpectedly walk onto the road
Sometimes they turn back half-way across

correct_answers.text: They will look neither left nor right
They will unexpectedly walk onto the road
Sometimes they turn back half-way across

comment: Zebra crossings have a protective function for pedestrians. They give them priority over other road users. Some pedestrians thoughtlessly trust this protection and cross the roadway without paying attention to the traffic. At zebra crossings, be aware that pedestrians and especially elderly or vulnerable people may enter the roadway without looking left and right. It is also possible that pedestrians will turn halfway around when the traffic lights turn red.

question_text:
A pedestrian with a white stick wants to cross the road in front of you. What should you do?
I have to

options.text: - reduce speed and stop if necessary
- give a warning signal
- continue driving at the same speed

correct_answers.text: - reduce speed and stop if necessary

comment: The white cane shows you that this road user is blind or at least severely visually impaired. The stick is also the sign that the person is allowed to participate in road traffic without an escort. You must always treat blind and visually impaired people with increased consideration. Reduce your speed and stop if necessary. Do not honk: you would frighten and unsettle the person.

question_text: What should you anticipate?

options.text: That pedestrians will walk onto the road in front of me
That children will suddenly appear between the vehicles
That pedestrians will wait until I have driven past

correct_answers.text: That pedestrians will walk onto the road in front of me
That children will suddenly appear between the vehicles

comment: The "Children" danger sign on the right warns you to take extra care. With many parked vehicles, however, you must always assume that people will step onto the carriageway unexpectedly. Of course, in addition to children, adults can also fail to behave in a roadworthy manner and suddenly appear between the vehicles.

question_text: What should you anticipate?

options.text: That pedestrians will suddenly walk onto the road
That doors of vehicles will be opened
That vehicles will begin moving

correct_answers.text: That pedestrians will suddenly walk onto the road
That doors of vehicles will be opened
That vehicles will begin moving

comment: In a traffic situation with several parked vehicles and different road users, the parked vehicles impair your visibility. Pedestrians can be expected to emerge between cars to cross the road. It is also possible for people to get out of vehicles or for vehicles to drive off without paying attention to the current traffic situation.

question_text: What is your assessment of this situation?

options.text: The female pedestrian may walk unheedingly onto the road
The pedestrian with the moped may change direction suddenly
I can continue driving at the same speed

correct_answers.text: The female pedestrian may walk unheedingly onto the road
The pedestrian with the moped may change direction suddenly

comment: You should only pass the waiting pedestrian at the side of the road with an appropriate safe distance and very carefully. The same applies to a moped rider who is properly pushing his moped on the right-hand side of the road. If necessary, you can also change to the left lane.

question_text: A person at the side of the road is wearing a yellow armband with three black spots. What does this armband indicate?

options.text: The wearer is disabled
I am obliged to behave in a particular way towards this person
This person belongs to a particular profession

correct_answers.text: The wearer is disabled
I am obliged to behave in a particular way towards this person

comment: If you see a person at the side of the road wearing a yellow armband with three black dots, this means for you: the principle of trust has been suspended. You now have an increased duty of care. This is because the armband indicates a physical limitation in the form of a severe visual impairment. If visually impaired persons wear this armband and/or a white stick, they are allowed to move in traffic without an escort.

question_text:
Why do you have to reduce your speed here?
Because of the

options.text: - child
- motorbike
- [SUV]

correct_answers.text: - child

comment: If a van is parked in front of a house and a child runs out of the house, the child may run into the road directly in front of the van. Children rarely pay attention to traffic. Therefore, you should be able to brake immediately in an emergency. To do this, you should reduce your driving speed.

question_text:
What should you anticipate when pedestrians are crossing the road?
Pedestrians can

options.text: - be inattentive
- come to a sudden stop
- turn back, after half-way

correct_answers.text: - be inattentive
- come to a sudden stop
- turn back, after half-way

comment: When a pedestrian crosses the roadway, it is not certain that he will continue this action to the opposite side of the road. It is also quite possible that he will stop, turn around or continue with a delay.

question_text: Why must you drive slowly now, and be ready to brake?

options.text: Because of the pedestrian
Because the bus is moving off
Because [of the cyclist]

correct_answers.text: Because of the pedestrian

comment: You must drive slowly and be ready to brake because passengers can cross the road in front of the bus.

question_text:
Why are you required to brake here?
Because of the

options.text: - child
- cyclist
- [green] vehicle

correct_answers.text: - child

comment: A child is behind the parked vehicle and will probably cross the road in the next moment.

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I reduce my speed
Ich ready myself for an emergency braking manoeuvre
I continue driving as before

correct_answers.text: I reduce my speed
Ich ready myself for an emergency braking manoeuvre

comment: Since the dog, most likely, will run onto the street from the left, you have to reduce your speed and prepare for a braking for danger.

question_text: Why are you required to stop here?

options.text: Because [a pedestrian] wants to cross the road from the left
